lessons.title: Nutritional Requirements of Farmed Fish
lessons.body:
Fish need six main nutrients: protein, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water. Protein is the most critical for growth. For tilapia, a common farmed fish in Africa, fingerlings need 35-40% protein in their feed, while adults need 28-32%. Catfish require even more: 40-45% for fry, 35-40% for adults. If you feed too little protein, fish grow slowly and you waste money on feed. Too much protein is also wasteful because fish cannot store it and excrete it as ammonia, which pollutes water.

Carbohydrates are cheaper energy sources. Tilapia can use up to 40% carbohydrates in their diet, but catfish handle only 20-25%. Fats provide concentrated energy and essential fatty acids. A good feed has 5-10% fat. Vitamins and minerals are needed in tiny amounts but are vital for health and bone formation. In Africa, many farmers use agricultural by-products like rice bran, maize bran, and cassava peels. These are good energy sources but low in protein. To meet protein needs, you must add protein-rich ingredients like fishmeal, soybean meal, or cottonseed meal.

Water quality affects nutrition too. If water is too cold (below 20Â°C), fish eat less and digest slowly. In warm African climates (25-30Â°C), fish eat more and grow faster. So feed according to temperature and fish size. A practical rule: check your fish weekly. If they are not growing, adjust protein or feeding rate. Local feed mills often sell pellets with guaranteed analysis on the bag. Read the label: it tells you protein, fat, and fibre percentages. Choose feed that matches your fish species and age. Remember, underfeeding causes stunted growth, but overfeeding wastes money and fouls water.

lessons.title: Types of Fish Feed: Commercial and Farm-Made
lessons.body:
Commercial fish feed comes in three forms: sinking pellets, floating pellets, and crumbles. Floating pellets are best for tilapia because you can see if they eat. Sinking pellets suit catfish that feed at the bottom. Crumbles are for fry and fingerlings. In Africa, brands like Aller Aqua, Skretting, and local mills like Raanan Fish Feed (Nigeria) or Kenya's Unga Farm Care sell feeds. A 20 kg bag of 30% protein tilapia feed costs about $25-40, depending on country. Commercial feed is convenient and balanced, but expensive. Many small-scale farmers cannot afford it alone.

Farm-made feed is cheaper but requires careful mixing. You can make feed using locally available ingredients: fishmeal (from local fish processing waste), soybean meal, maize bran, rice bran, cassava flour, and vitamin premix. A simple recipe for tilapia grow-out: 30% fishmeal, 30% soybean meal, 35% maize bran, 5% vitamin/mineral premix. Mix dry ingredients, then add water to make a dough. Pass through a mincer or meat grinder to form pellets. Sun-dry for 1-2 days until moisture is below 10%. Store in sacks away from damp.

Farm-made feed has risks: nutrient levels vary, and mixing may be inconsistent. Always use a scale, not cups. A 20 kg batch should have exactly 6 kg fishmeal, 6 kg soybean meal, etc. If you cannot get fishmeal, use more soybean meal but add 1% methionine (an amino acid) because soybean lacks it. For catfish, increase fishmeal to 40%. Also, consider using black soldier fly larvae (BSF) as a protein source. You can raise BSF on kitchen waste; dried larvae contain 40-45% protein. Many African farmers now use BSF to cut feed costs by 30%. Whether commercial or farm-made, the key is consistency and meeting the fish's protein needs.

lessons.title: Feed Formulation and Ingredient Selection
lessons.body:
Feed formulation means mixing ingredients to meet specific nutrient targets. Start with a Pearson Square method for simplicity. Suppose you want a 30% protein feed using fishmeal (60% protein) and maize bran (10% protein). Draw a square, put 60 on left top, 10 on left bottom, and 30 in the centre. Subtract diagonally: 60-30=30, 30-10=20. So you need 20 parts fishmeal and 30 parts maize bran. That gives 40% fishmeal and 60% maize bran. But that's too much fishmeal; you can substitute part with soybean meal (44% protein). Use trial and error with a calculator or free app like Feed Formulation (available on Google Play).

Ingredient selection depends on cost and availability. In Africa, common ingredients: fishmeal (60-65% protein), soybean meal (44-48%), groundnut cake (40-45%), cottonseed meal (32-38%, but toxic gossypol must be limited to 10% of diet), sunflower cake (28-30%), maize (8-9%), maize bran (8-12%), rice bran (10-12%), cassava peels (2-3%), and palm kernel cake (15-18%). Also, use vitamin premix (1-2%) and mineral premix (1-2%). For catfish, replace some plant protein with fishmeal because catfish need more essential amino acids. A typical catfish diet: 40% fishmeal, 20% soybean meal, 30% maize bran, 5% vitamin premix, 5% fish oil.

Always test your feed. Mix a small batch, feed to a few fish in a hapa (net cage) for two weeks. Compare growth with commercial feed. If fish grow slower, adjust protein or add lysine and methionine. Also, check for anti-nutritional factors: raw soybean has trypsin inhibitor, so roast or cook soybeans before use. Cottonseed meal must be limited. Cassava peels should be sun-dried to remove cyanide. Use a hammer mill to grind ingredients to fine powder (less than 1 mm) for better digestion. Store ingredients in dry, ventilated place. Buy in bulk to reduce cost. Join a farmer cooperative to share purchases and formulation costs.

lessons.title: Feeding Strategies and Ration Calculation
lessons.body:
Feeding strategy determines how much, how often, and when you feed. Overfeeding wastes money and pollutes water; underfeeding stunts growth. The daily ration is a percentage of fish body weight. For tilapia: fry (0.5-5 g) eat 10-15% of body weight per day; fingerlings (5-20 g) eat 6-8%; adults (over 50 g) eat 2-3%. For catfish: fry eat 8-10%, adults 1-2%. To calculate: weigh a sample of 10 fish, get average weight, multiply by number of fish to get total biomass. Then multiply by feeding rate. Example: 1000 tilapia averaging 100 g = 100 kg biomass. At 3% feeding rate, feed 3 kg per day. Split into two meals: 1.5 kg morning and 1.5 kg evening.

Feed at fixed times daily. Tilapia feed best in morning (8-10 am) and afternoon (3-5 pm). Catfish feed more at dusk and night. Use floating pellets for tilapia so you can see when they stop eating. Stop feeding when they no longer come to surface. For catfish, use sinking pellets and check after 30 minutes; remove uneaten feed to avoid fouling. Adjust feeding based on water temperature: if below 20Â°C, reduce by half; if above 32Â°C, also reduce because oxygen is low. In Africa, many farms have rainy and dry seasons. During heavy rain, fish eat less. During dry season, watch for low water levels and high ammonia.

Keep records. Write down daily feed amount, fish behaviour, and water temperature. Every two weeks, sample weigh 10 fish. If average weight gain is less than expected (e.g., tilapia should gain 2-3 g per day in optimal conditions), increase feed slightly or check for disease. A simple tool: a hanging scale (5 kg capacity) and a bucket. For small ponds, use a feeding tray to check consumption. Never feed mouldy or expired feed. If feed smells sour, discard. Also, train fish to eat at a specific spot by tapping the water before feeding. This reduces waste. In integrated systems (e.g., with chickens), chicken manure can fertilise pond water to grow natural fish food, reducing feed needs by 20-30%.

lessons.title: Feed Storage and Quality Control
lessons.body:
Feed storage is critical because poor storage kills nutrients and grows mould. Mould produces aflatoxin, which can poison fish and humans who eat the fish. Store feed in a cool, dry, dark place. Ideal temperature: below 25Â°C. Humidity should be below 12%. In many African villages, this means a raised wooden platform inside a ventilated room, not on the floor. Use pallets to keep bags off the ground. Keep bags away from walls to allow air circulation. Never store feed near chemicals like fuel, pesticides, or fertiliser because fish feed absorbs odours and toxins.

Use airtight containers for farm-made feed. Plastic drums with lids or metal silos work well. For commercial feed, keep in original bags and seal tightly after opening. A 50 kg bag opened should be used within 2-4 weeks. If you buy in bulk, use first-in, first-out. Label each bag with date of purchase or production. Check feed before use: smell it (should smell fresh, not musty), look for clumps or mould (white or green patches), and feel for dampness. If feed is damp, dry it in sun for a few hours but not too long because sunlight destroys vitamins. Better to prevent dampness.

Quality control also means testing feed. You can do a simple water stability test: put a handful of pellets in a glass of water. Good pellets hold shape for at least 30 minutes. If they disintegrate quickly, they will foul water. For protein content, you cannot test at home, but you can send a sample to a laboratory (e.g., at a university or agricultural research station). In Kenya, KALRO offers feed analysis for about $20 per sample. For farm-made feed, ensure ingredients are fresh. Never use mouldy maize or rancid fishmeal. Store fishmeal in freezer if possible. Add mould inhibitor like propionic acid (0.5%) to farm-made feed if storing more than one month. Also, keep rodents and insects out. Use traps or cats. A well-stored feed retains nutrients for 3-6 months. If you see weevils, discard the feed. Remember: cheap feed that is spoiled is more expensive than good feed.

lessons.title: Reducing Feed Waste and Cost
lessons.body:
Feed is 60-70% of fish farming costs. Reducing waste directly increases profit. First, use the right feed size. Fry need crumbles (0.5-1 mm), fingerlings need 1-2 mm pellets, and adults need 3-5 mm pellets. If pellets are too big, fish cannot eat them; too small, they dissolve before eating. Second, feed only what fish can consume in 20-30 minutes. For tilapia, feed until they stop coming to surface. For catfish, feed 80% of what they would eat in 30 minutes. Use a feeding tray or a fixed feeding spot to monitor. Third, avoid overfeeding. Many farmers feed 5% body weight when 3% is enough. Weigh feed with a kitchen scale, not by hand.

Use alternative protein sources. Black soldier fly (BSF) larvae can replace 30-50% of fishmeal. You can raise BSF in a box with kitchen waste. A 1 mÂ² BSF bin produces 1-2 kg of larvae per week. Dry them and grind into meal. Also, use agricultural by-products: brewers' spent grain (20-25% protein), palm kernel cake, and cassava peels. But balance with protein concentrates. Another way: fertilise your pond. Add chicken manure (500 kg per hectare per week) or cow dung (1 ton per hectare per week) to grow natural plankton. This reduces commercial feed by 20-30%. For tilapia, plankton is excellent food.

Improve feed conversion ratio (FCR). FCR = feed given / fish weight gain. Good FCR for tilapia is 1.5-2.0; for catfish 1.2-1.5. If your FCR is above 2.5, you are wasting feed. To improve FCR: maintain good water quality (oxygen above 5 mg/L, ammonia below 0.5 mg/L), keep stocking density moderate (3-5 fish per mÂ² for tilapia), and harvest at optimal size. Also, store feed properly to avoid spoilage. Buy feed in bulk with other farmers to get discounts. Make your own feed using a hammer mill and mixer (cost: $500-1000, but pays back in one season). Finally, keep records: track feed used and fish harvested. If you see waste, adjust. A simple rule: every kilogram of feed saved is profit.

quiz.q: What is the recommended protein percentage for adult tilapia feed?
quiz.explanation: Adult tilapia need 28-32% protein for maintenance and growth.

quiz.q: Which fish species requires higher protein in its diet?
quiz.explanation: Catfish require 35-40% protein as adults, higher than tilapia.

quiz.q: What is a common sign of overfeeding in fish ponds?
options: B) Water becomes cloudy and smelly
quiz.explanation: Overfeeding leads to uneaten feed decomposing, causing poor water quality.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is a good plant-based protein source for fish feed?
quiz.explanation: Soybean meal contains 44-48% protein, much higher than the other options.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of floating pellets for tilapia?
options: B) You can see if fish are eating
C) They sink to the bottom
quiz.explanation: Floating pellets allow farmers to observe feeding activity and adjust ration.

quiz.q: Which of these is a risk of farm-made feed?
quiz.explanation: Without precise mixing, farm-made feed may not meet exact nutrient requirements.

quiz.q: What is the Pearson Square used for?
options: B) Formulating feed to a target protein level
quiz.explanation: The Pearson Square is a simple method to blend two ingredients to achieve a desired protein percentage.

quiz.q: Which ingredient should be limited to 10% in fish feed due to toxicity?
quiz.explanation: Cottonseed meal contains gossypol, which is toxic to fish at high levels.

quiz.q: What is the daily feeding rate for adult tilapia (over 50g)?
quiz.explanation: Adult tilapia are typically fed 2-3% of their total biomass per day.

quiz.q: How often should you sample weigh fish to adjust feeding?
quiz.explanation: Biweekly sampling helps track growth and adjust ration accurately.

quiz.q: What is a good feeding time for tilapia?
quiz.explanation: Tilapia feed best in the morning and afternoon when oxygen levels are adequate.

quiz.q: What should you do if uneaten feed remains after 30 minutes in catfish ponds?
quiz.explanation: Removing uneaten feed prevents water pollution and waste.

quiz.q: What is the ideal moisture content for stored fish feed?
quiz.explanation: Moisture below 12% prevents mould growth and aflatoxin production.

quiz.q: Which storage practice helps prevent feed spoilage?
options: C) Store on raised pallets in a dry room
quiz.explanation: Raised pallets and dry conditions reduce moisture and pest problems.

quiz.q: What is aflatoxin?
quiz.explanation: Aflatoxin is a poisonous substance produced by moulds on poorly stored feed.

quiz.q: How can you test feed water stability at home?
options: A) Put pellets in water and see how long they hold shape
quiz.explanation: Good pellets should remain intact in water for at least 30 minutes.

quiz.q: What is the first-in, first-out rule for feed storage?
options: D) Store feed in random order
quiz.explanation: Using older feed first prevents spoilage and waste.

quiz.q: What is the recommended protein range for catfish fry?
quiz.explanation: Catfish fry require 40-45% protein for rapid growth.

quiz.q: Which of these is a cost-saving strategy in fish feeding?
options: B) Using black soldier fly larvae
C) Buying expensive commercial feed only
quiz.explanation: Black soldier fly larvae can replace up to 50% of fishmeal, reducing feed costs.

quiz.q: What is feed conversion ratio (FCR)?
options: A) Feed given divided by fish weight gain
B) Fish weight divided by feed given
D) Number of fish per pond
quiz.explanation: FCR measures how efficiently fish convert feed into body weight.

quiz.q: What is a good FCR for tilapia?
quiz.explanation: An FCR of 1.5-2.0 means 1.5-2 kg of feed produces 1 kg of fish.

quiz.q: How can pond fertilisation reduce feed costs?
options: B) It grows natural plankton that fish eat
quiz.explanation: Fertilising with manure promotes plankton growth, providing natural food for tilapia.

quiz.q: What is the recommended feeding rate for tilapia fingerlings (5-20g)?
quiz.explanation: Fingerlings need 6-8% of body weight daily for optimal growth.

quiz.q: Which vitamin or mineral premix percentage is typical in farm-made feed?
quiz.explanation: A 1-2% inclusion of vitamin/mineral premix meets micronutrient needs.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid storing feed near pesticides?
options: A) Pesticides make feed taste better
D) It is not a problem
quiz.explanation: Feed can absorb harmful chemicals from pesticides, poisoning fish.

quiz.q: What is the benefit of using a feeding tray?
options: B) It helps monitor feed consumption
C) It makes fish grow slower
D) It is only for catfish
quiz.explanation: A feeding tray allows you to see how much feed is eaten and adjust ration.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of poor quality feed?
quiz.explanation: Mould indicates spoilage and potential aflatoxin contamination.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of adding propionic acid to farm-made feed?
quiz.explanation: Propionic acid acts as a mould inhibitor, extending feed shelf life.

quiz.q: How much can black soldier fly larvae replace fishmeal in fish diets?
quiz.explanation: BSF larvae can replace 30-50% of fishmeal without harming growth.

quiz.q: What is the first step in making farm-made fish feed?
options: B) Grinding dry ingredients into fine powder
quiz.explanation: Grinding ensures uniform particle size for proper pellet formation and digestion.
